methodological_rigor.justification: The retrospective multicenter cohort is reasonably well defined, the response endpoint is explicit, and the IMC workflow includes segmentation, clustering, and a patient-level train/test split for the GA-MIL model. The main limitation is scale: only 82 samples entered the spatial analysis and just 10 patients formed the independent test set, so the model estimates are necessarily unstable. The authors acknowledge the exploratory nature of the work, which is appropriate, but the evidence remains preliminary.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort study, so Oxford level 2b applies. The clinical relevance is fairly direct because the paper addresses BCG response and progression in high-risk NMIBC, which affects treatment escalation and cystectomy decisions. Even though the findings are exploratory, they map onto a real preoperative decision point and are not limited to mechanistic interest.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE fits the retrospective human cohort and the manuscript gives unusually detailed methodological description for the IMC pipeline, clinical endpoint definitions, and patient-level splitting. It also flags key limitations, including small sample size, TMA sampling, and lack of orthogonal validation. The reproducibility posture is weaker because there is no public dataset or code repository, and the work relies on a very small hold-out set.

novelty_literature.justification: The combination of spatial single-cell IMC and an IMC-specific gated-attention MIL classifier for BCG response is a genuinely novel configuration in bladder cancer. The manuscript also positions its findings against the BRS3 transcriptomic subtype, adding a coherent biological frame. It is not first-in-kind across all of spatial pathology or MIL, but it is a credible new combination in this disease setting.

writing_presentation.justification: The paper is clearly organized and the abstract accurately summarizes the cohort, the spatial findings, and the predictive model. The discussion is long but generally coherent, and it does a good job tying the IMC findings back to known BCG biology. The main writing drawback is length rather than clarity; the manuscript is dense, but not disorganized.

key_strengths: Addresses a clinically important question in BCG-treated NMIBC with a clear endpoint definition.
Combines spatial single-cell profiling with a patient-level attention-based classifier.
Includes multicenter tissue sampling and a biologically plausible interpretation anchored to BRS3-like biology.
Reports the limitations of the small test set and exploratory nature explicitly.
key_concerns: The independent test set is only 10 patients, so the model performance is fragile.
There is no external validation cohort or orthogonal confirmation of the main spatial signatures.
TMA-based sampling may miss heterogeneity and the paper itself notes pre-analytical concerns.
No public data or code resource is provided for reuse.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a good exploratory translational biomarker paper, but the predictive claim is still early and needs more validation. A tier-3 journal could plausibly take it after major revisions focused on robustness and external confirmation.
